metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL MySQL OTel] High memory utilization
metadata.description: Alerts when the average memory utilization of a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance over the last 15 minutes is at least 95% of its memory quota (database/memory/utilization taken once per minute and averaged over at least 5 observed minutes, so duplicate points don't skew it). A warm InnoDB buffer pool keeps memory high but flat, which is normal. This threshold sits above that steady state, close to the point where MySQL risks an out-of-memory restart.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_mysql.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// Per instance and minute: memory utilization (fraction of the instance memory quota), plus the MySQL marker.
// One value per minute collapses duplicate points from overlapping series, so every observed minute counts once.
| STATS memory = AVG(AVG_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/memory/utilization`)),
        memory_max = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/memory/utilization`)),
        marker = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/queries`))
  BY `@timestamp` = TBUCKET(1 minute), database_id
// Mean and peak over the observed minutes
| STATS avg_memory = AVG(memory),
        mem_peak = MAX(memory_max),
        observed_minutes = COUNT(memory),
        marker = SUM(marker)
  BY database_id

data.content:
## Cloud SQL MySQL high memory utilization

Memory use has averaged at least 95% of the instance's quota for about 15 minutes. Cloud SQL can restart the instance when it runs out of memory.

### Triage
1. Open **[GCP OTel] Cloud SQL MySQL Instance Detail**, then *Memory usage vs quota*. Steady growth toward the quota is the risk; a high but flat line is the normal buffer pool.
2. Correlate with connections (*Connections vs max connections*): each connection allocates per-thread buffers, so connection surges drive memory up.
3. Look for large sorts, joins or temporary tables, and for recently raised flags such as `innodb_buffer_pool_size`, `sort_buffer_size`, `join_buffer_size` or `tmp_table_size`.

### Actions
Reduce the connection count (pooling), lower oversized per-session buffers, kill memory-heavy queries, or move to a tier with more memory.

### Tuning
Change `avg_memory >= 0.95` to adjust the threshold. A value of 0.9 gives an earlier warning on instances whose steady state is lower.
